::: {.why}
Half the transformations in your notebooks are window functions, and writing them where the data lives is faster, shorter and the version an interviewer will ask you to produce.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Write a rolling aggregate per symbol as a window function and explain the frame clause.
- Say when computing in SQL beats pulling into pandas, in terms of what crosses the process boundary.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Work through the window functions material on Modern SQL, then write four queries against your own DuckDB store: a 20-day rolling mean per symbol, a rank within each date, a lagged value per symbol, and a cumulative sum reset at each year. Get the partition and frame clauses right rather than approximately right.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Measure the boundary: time each query computed in SQL against the equivalent pulled into pandas, for a full universe over ten years. Report both times and the peak memory. The gap is mostly serialisation, and knowing that is what tells you which side of the boundary a computation belongs on.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Four window-function queries against your store, each timed against its pandas equivalent with peak memory reported.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Write a query that computes a 20-day rolling mean per symbol from a trades table, then say why doing it in SQL might be the right call.
:::
